high.title: Foreign investors have explosive net selling of nearly 7.2 trillion VND in first week of June, which stocks are in focus?
high.summary: In the first week of June, the Vietnamese stock market faced strong net selling pressure right from the opening session, quickly losing the 1,870-point mark. VN-Index fell 24.59 points (-1.23%) week-on-week to close at 1,838.9 points. Foreign investors continued massive selling pressure with 7.192 trillion VND net selling across the entire market over 5 sessions. On HoSE specifically, foreigners net sold 7.342 trillion VND. VIC was the most heavily sold stock with 4.820 trillion VND in net selling. This represents significant capital outflow that could pressure VND and indicates foreign investor sentiment toward Vietnamese equities. The selling was particularly concentrated in Thursday's session with nearly 5.8 trillion VND net selling, mainly through block transactions. Banking stocks and Vingroup provided some support in the final two sessions, but the overall trend shows continued foreign divestment from Vietnamese markets.

high.title: A securities company newly listed just entered FTSE Vietnam ETF in June restructuring
high.summary: In the Q2/2026 review on June 5, FTSE Russell added VPS Securities (VCK) to the FTSE Vietnam Index basket while removing DIG, DGC, and GAS. The new portfolio takes effect after Friday's close (June 19) and officially trades from Monday (June 22). However, there are no longer any funds tracking the FTSE Vietnam Index after the Xtrackers FTSE Vietnam Swap UCITS ETF changed its name and reference index in September. The fund now tracks the STOXX Vietnam Total Market Liquid index instead, reducing the significance of FTSE Vietnam Index changes for Vietnamese markets.

high.title: Bank employee offers savings rate nearly 9%/year despite only listing maximum rate over 6%
high.summary: The deposit mobilization race among banks is intensifying with special interest rate programs for large deposits. A VPBank branch employee offered online savings rates up to 8.9%/year for 6-9 month terms for deposits of 50 billion VND or more, significantly higher than the 6%+ publicly listed rates. For deposits of 100-300 million VND, rates reach 8.3%/year. This aggressive deposit competition indicates banks' liquidity needs and could signal upward pressure on overall interest rates, which would be positive for VND but potentially negative for government bond prices as bank deposit rates compete with bond yields.

medium.title: Savings interest rates 6/6: Latest rate table from Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
medium.summary: MBV currently has the highest deposit rates on the market at 7%/year for terms from 6-18 months. PGBank and VIB also list 7%/year for 12-month terms. State-owned banks (Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, VietinBank) are offering 6.8%/year for online deposits of 12 months or more. This rate environment shows continued competition for deposits and upward pressure on funding costs.

medium.title: SJC gold and plain gold ring prices on 6/6: Continue sharp decline, some brands down 4.6 million VND/tael
medium.summary: Gold prices in Vietnam continued falling sharply following global market declines, with SJC gold bars trading at 146.2-150.2 million VND/tael (buy-sell), down 3 million VND from previous levels. DOJI saw the biggest drop of 4.6 million VND/tael on buying price. The sharp gold price decline reflects global risk-off sentiment and could indicate reduced inflation pressures that might influence monetary policy.

medium.title: Tax Department clarifies information about "dropping proposal for banks to provide taxpayer account information"
medium.summary: The Tax Department clarified that requirements for credit institutions to provide taxpayer account information to tax authorities remain in the draft decree. This regulation would require banks to cooperate with tax authorities when detecting unusual transactions needing tax compliance checks, potentially affecting banking operations and customer privacy.

medium.title: Over 4.4 million customer instances received warnings, stopped over 5,000 billion VND in transactions
medium.summary: Deputy Governor Pham Thanh Ha announced that the banking sector has made significant achievements in promoting digital payments and building a modern digital ecosystem. The warning system helped prevent over 5 trillion VND in potentially fraudulent transactions, demonstrating the effectiveness of digital banking security measures and supporting the goal of increasing non-cash payment value to 30 times GDP by 2030.
